I will keep the year simple and familiar: I will grow winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, where wheat in spring and a wheat-maize annual rotation fit the local weather and water pattern well. The local pattern is clear from Quzhou and North China Plain sources: winter wheat is the main crop in spring in Quzhou, more than 80% of fields there are in winter wheat-summer maize rotation, and most rain comes in the maize season while wheat needs more irrigation ([Gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/policywatch/202403/20/content_WS65fa42b6c6d0868f4e8e5435.html), [PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/), [ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0048969721021094)). Because I am 67 and I have no reason to make the year harder than it needs to be, I will not split my land into many crops. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, keep fertilizer moderate instead of chasing the highest possible input, irrigate wheat twice and maize once if needed, and rely on machine work where timing is tight. I will rotary-till before wheat after maize harvest, and I will direct-seed or no-till maize right after wheat harvest so I do not lose moisture or time. My goal is steady grain, manageable labor, and lower risk rather than doing anything fancy.
